subject: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.jordan@example.com, sourcing@talentbridge.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)

Hi team —

We have Alex Jordan progressing to on-site interviews for the Senior Serving Engineer role. I put together a proposed slate and short role scope so we can align on what we should be evaluating. Please review and reply with any objections or swaps by EOD today; we’ll lock the calendar tomorrow.

Role scope (short):
- Owning inference runtime features: latency SLOs, batching, caching strategies, kernel selection logic.
- Building infra for model slicing, rollout, and graceful degradation.
- Cross-team work with product / SRE to ship performance SLAs.

Proposed interview slate (60m blocks):
1) System design (ben) — distributed serving, SLO tradeoffs, throughput planning
2) Model runtime deep dive (vivek) — attention/kv cache, kernel selection, perf optimizations
3) Debugging / incident simulation (laura) — on-call troubleshooting, triage stories
4) Behavioral / scope / collaboration (marissa) — drive, ownership, ambiguous problems

Leveling expectations I want us all on the same page for:
- Senior: clear ownership of a component with multiple teams, shipped performance improvements with measurable impact (~20-40% cost/latency), can lead design reviews but still pairs with staff for cross-org architecture.

Attachments: I’ve attached the latest Interview_Rubric_v2.docx and Alex’s resume (from sourcing).

Questions for panel:
- Do we want a coding exercise? (I’m inclined to skip a live algorithm whiteboard for this role; prefer system-level and runtime deep dive)
- Any specific red flags to watch in behavioral? (e.g., lack of ownership across multi-team projects)

Thanks — I’ll consolidate and set the slots.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Group Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, alex.jordan@example.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)

Ben —

Thanks for the slate. Quick thoughts:
- I agree with the non-coding emphasis. For the debugging exercise, can we formalize a short post-mortem prompt (15m to discuss) that surfaces incident ownership and RCA depth? That helps compare candidates consistently.
- Suggest swapping the order so runtime deep dive comes first (it’ll prime their technical vocabulary) followed by system design.
- I think we should add a short 15-minute structured rubric check-in between panelists after interviews to capture immediate impressions (can be a Google Form).

Minor: in your leveling bullets, add explicit expectation around mentoring (senior should have at least 1-2 mentees and run small technical reviews).

I’m ok to take the debugging block if that helps.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Staff Engineer, Reliability

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: alex.jordan@example.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)

Quick notes from a bar-raiser perspective:
- For runtime deep dive, focus on tradeoffs candidates make for KV cache invalidation, prefix caching strategies, and how they measure end-to-end impact (not just microbenchmarks). Ask them for a concrete experiment they ran and what metrics they used.
- On leveling: senior should be able to reason about cross-regional routing and fallback policies. If they can't articulate fallback strategies under capacity pressure, that's a concern.
- I support the 15-minute form after each interview to reduce recency bias. We should include a hard yes/no "meets bar" checkbox + one-sentence rationale.

I’ll take the runtime deep dive. Ben — can you include one concrete system prompt we can use for consistent questioning?

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Principal Inference Engineer (Bar-raiser)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@example.com>, sourcing@talentbridge.com
Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)

Folks — scheduling update and candidate materials:
- Alex is available for an on-site loop on Tue 25 May between 09:00-13:00 PT and prefers morning slots.
- I attached Alex’s resume (Resume_Alex_Jordan.pdf) and a short writeup the candidate provided on a recent perf improvement.
- Sourcing also confirmed a 30-minute pre-read call with Alex on Mon 24 May at 10:00 PT; I’ll send that calendar invite.

Action items:
- Please confirm you can take the morning slots on Tue 25 May. If you want to swap order as Laura suggested (runtime -> system design -> debugging -> behavioral), I can rearrange calendar invites.
- I’ll create the 15-minute post-interview feedback form and share the link before the loop.

Attachments: Resume_Alex_Jordan.pdf, Candidate_Writeup_AJ.pdf

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Talent Partner

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: Alex Jordan <alex.jordan@example.com>, sourcing@talentbridge.com
Date: Sun, 22 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interview slate + panel roles for Senior Serving Engineer (scope + leveling)

Thanks everyone — this looks good. Locked plan and next steps:

Final slate (Tue 25 May, morning):
- 09:00-10:00 PT: Runtime deep dive (Vivek) — focus on prefix caching, KV cache invalidation, metrics to prove impact.
- 10:15-11:15 PT: System design (Ben) — cross-region routing, graceful degradation, throughput targeting.
- 11:30-12:30 PT: Debugging / incident simulation (Laura) — PM-style incident prompt; candidate to present troubleshooting approach.
- 12:45-13:15 PT: Behavioral / collaboration (Marissa) — scope, mentorship, cross-team partnerships.

Rubric & leveling bullets: don’t forget mentoring expectation I suggested, plus the fallback strategy item Vivek raised. I updated the Interview_Rubric_v2.docx with two short fields: "Mentoring & Scope" and "Fallback/Degradation Reasoning" (link to Drive in metadata).

Marissa — please send calendar invites and the post-interview feedback form link. Vivek — I’ll email you a short runtime prompt by tomorrow morning to use across interviews.

I’ll run the calibration sync if we need a quick 15-minute chat after the loop to decide next steps. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Group Hiring Manager, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
